title: Approve a retention and erasure schedule for the user and secrets collections
description: Draft and approve a retention schedule covering every column of db-models-mongodb.default.user and db-models-mongodb.default.secrets as classified in company-profile/example-co/sdlc/metastore.json. For each data class state: the retention period and its governing law (SEBI stock-broker/DP record-keeping, PMLA section 12 and RBI KYC Master Direction five years after the relationship ends, DPDP Rules 8(3) one-year minimum); the erasure trigger (consent withdrawal, account closure, broker disconnection, access-token expiry); and erase versus anonymise. Broker credentials (zerodha_password, zerodha_2fa, apiSecrets, accessToken) must have a short expiry tied to the session or connection, not account life. The schedule is the input to tasks 2-4 and satisfies the documented-policy half of SEBI CSCRF PR.AA.S13.
acceptanceCriteria: A signed retention schedule exists, with a period, legal basis, erasure trigger and erase/anonymise decision for every column of the user and secrets collections listed in sdlc/metastore.json
The schedule sets an explicit maximum lifetime for Secrets.accessToken, zerodha_password, zerodha_2fa and apiSecrets, and a post-closure retention period for User PII
The CISO and DPO have both recorded approval of the schedule, with a date, before task 2 starts

verificationMethod.description: Compliance reviews the approved schedule against the column list for user and secrets in sdlc/metastore.json. Expected: no column is missing a retention period and erasure trigger, each period cites its governing law, and the approval is signed and dated.

rootCause.description: No data-retention and disposal schedule was ever defined for client PII and connected-broker credentials, so engineers had no retention period or erasure trigger to implement in the models.
